newsitem.title: FRANCE: French National Assembly approves pension funds.
newsitem.headline: French National Assembly approves pension funds.

text.p: The National Assembly on Friday approved a bill to introduce private pension funds in France, promising a boon for the stock market and prising open France's traditional state-backed retirement system.
The RPR and UDF governing coalition partners voted in favour and the Socialist and Communists against.

The text adopted allows for income tax write-offs for contributors capped at five percent of gross salary and also for lump sum payouts of 20 percent of pension money with a limit of 100,000 francs ($19,720) and the rest payable in annuities.

The funds, which would be managed by banks and insurers and set up by joint agreement between employers and employees, will be able to invest a maximum of 65 percent in bonds, leaving the way open for hefty investment in equities.
The text now has to be examined by the Senate, the upper house of parliament.

The government has long insisted that the new funds will complement rather than replace the current system of universal pensions and Finance Minister Jean Arthuis hopes the new funds will be introduced as early as next year. ($1=5.070 French Franc)
